title: UPSC CSE - Quantitative Ability - Percentage and Ratio
subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: The increase in the price of a certain item was 25%. Then the price was decreased by 20% and then again increased by 10%. What is the resultant increase in the price?
questions.explain: Let the original price be 100. After a 25% increase, the price becomes 125. After a 20% decrease, the price becomes 100. The 10% increase makes it 110. The increase from the original is 10%.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: When 70% of a number x is added to another number y, the sum becomes 165% of the value of y. When 60% of the number x is added to another number z, then the sum becomes 165% of the value of z. Which one of the following is correct?
questions.explain: From the equations 0.7x + y = 1.65y and 0.6x + z = 1.65z, we can deduce relationships between x, y, and z, leading to z < x < y.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: Two candidates X and Y contested an election. 80% of voters cast their vote and there were no invalid votes. There was no NOTA (None of the above) option. X got 56% of the votes cast and won by 1440 votes. What is the total number of voters in the voters list?
questions.explain: Let total votes = V. Votes cast = 0.8V. X votes = 0.56 * 0.8V = 0.448V; Y votes = 0.52 * 0.8V = 0.352V. The margin of victory is 1440, so 0.096V = 1440, hence V = 15000.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: A pie chart gives the expenditure on five different items A, B, C, D and E in a household. If B, C, D and E correspond to 90 degree, 50, 45 and 75 respectively, then what is the percentage of expenditure on item A?
questions.explain: Angle for B is 90 degrees (25%). C is 50 degrees (5/18 of the total). D is 45 degrees (2.5/12). E is 75 degrees. Hence, A = 100 - (25 + 5/18 + 2.5/12 + 75)/ N.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: In a class, 60% of students are from India and 50% of the students are girls. If 30% of the Indian students are girls, then what percentage of foreign students are boys?
questions.explain: If 30% of Indian students are girls, then 70% are boys. If total girls are 50%, we assess the total of foreign students to find the ratio.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: A boy plays with a ball and he drops it from a height of 1.5 m. Every time the ball hits the ground, it bounces back to attain a height 4/5th of the previous height. The ball does not bounce further if the previous height is less than 50 cm. What is the number of times the ball hits the ground before the ball stops bouncing?
questions.explain: 1.5, 1.2, 0.96, 0.768, 0.6144, 0.49152 (this is the last bounce), hence 5 hits.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: A student appeared in 6 papers. The maximum marks are the same for each paper. His marks in these papers are in the proportion of 5: 6: 7: 8: 9: 10. Overall he scored 60%. In how many numbers of papers did he score less than 60% of the maximum marks?
questions.explain: The sums would require calculation based on proportions to ascertain marks below average across papers.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: An amount of money was distributed among A, B and C in the ratio p : q : r. Consider the following statements: 1. A gets the maximum share if p is greater than (q + r). 2. C gets the minimum share if r is less than (p + q). Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explain: If p > q+r, A has maximum share; if r < p+q, C's share cannot be minimum.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: A pie diagram shows the percentage distribution of proteins, water and other dry elements in the human body. Given that proteins correspond to 16% and water corresponds to 70%. If both proteins and the other dry elements correspond to p% then what is the central angle of the sector representing p on the pie diagram?
questions.explain: Water + Proteins = 86%, remaining p = 100% - 86% so 14%. In degrees, (14/100)*360 = 50.4. This does not fit options; however, central angle approximation helps.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: If the price of an article is decreased by 20% and then the new price is increased by 25%, then what is the net change in the price?
options: Cannot be determined due to insufficient data.
questions.explain: Let original price = 100. After decrease = 80, after increase = 100. Net change is 0%.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: A person bought a car and sold it for Rs. 3,00,000. If he incurred a loss of 20%, then how much did he spend to buy the car?
questions.explain: Selling Price = Cost Price - 0.20 Cost Price = 0.8 * Cost Price , cost price = 3,00,000/0.8 = 3,75,000.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: A shop owner offers the following discount options on an article to a customer: 1. Successive discounts of 10% and 20%, and then pay a service tax of 10% 2. Successive discounts of 20% and 10%, and then pay a service tax of 10% 3. Pay a service tax of 10% first, then successive discounts of 20% and 10%. Which one of the following is correct?
options: 1 only is the best option for the customer.
2 only is the best option for the customer.
3 only is the best option for the customer.
All the options are equally good for the customer.
questions.explain: Each follows a different method of discount, leading to equivalent results.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: In the adult Population of a city, 40% men and 30% women are married. What is the percentage of married adult population if no man marries more than one woman and no woman marries more than one man; and there are no widows and widowers?
questions.explain: Combined percentage of married adults will lead to ratios calculable from total adult population counts.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: A sum of Rs. 2,500 is distributed among X, Y and Z in the ratio 1/2: 3/4: 5/6. What is the difference between the maximum share and the minimum share?
questions.explain: Calculating the actual shares based on the provided ratio will lead to determining differences.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: As a result of a 25% hike in the price of rice per kg, a person is able to purchase 6 kg less rice for Rs. 1,200. What was the original price of rice per kg?
questions.explain: Formulate equation based on total available money and proportion differences due to hikes.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: A person X can complete 20% of work in 8 days and another person Y can complete 25% of the same work in 6 days. If they work together, in how many days will 40% of the work be completed?
questions.explain: Calculate work done per day and extrapolate to determine total days required.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: A and B are two heavy steel blocks. If B is placed on the top of A, the weight increases by 60%. How much weight will reduce with respect to the total weight of A and B, if B is removed from the top of A?
questions.explain: Analyze weight ratios and calculate based on total and individual contributions after repositioning.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: When a runner was crossing the 12 km mark, she was informed that she had completed only 80% of the race. How many kilometres was the runner supposed to run in this event?
questions.explain: Calculate total race distance considering 12 km is 80% of the total.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: Raju has Rs. 9000 with him and he wants to buy a mobile handset; but he finds that he has only 75% of the amount required to buy the handset. Therefore, he borrows 2000 from a friend. Then
options: Raju still does not have enough amount to buy the handset.
Raju has exactly the same amount as required to buy the handset.
Raju has enough amount to buy the handset and he will have 500 with him after buying the handset.
Raju has enough amount to buy the handset and he will have 1000 with him after buying the handset.
questions.explain: Calculate total funds after borrowing and determine against price.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: All members of a club went to Mumbai and stayed in a hotel on the first day, 80% went for shopping and 50% went for sightseeing, whereas 10% took rest in the hotel Which of the following conclusion(s) can be drawn from the above data?
options: 40% members went for shopping as well as sightseeing.
questions.explain: Calculate overlaps based on provided percentages using total club numbers.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: In a school, 60% students play cricket. A student who does not play cricket, plays football. Every football player has got a two-wheeler. Which of the following conclusions cannot be drawn from the above data?
options: 60% of the students do not have two-wheelers.
Cricket players do not play football.
questions.explain: Assess statements based on two-wheeler ownership versus sports player participation.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: The ratio of a two-digit natural number to a number formed by reversing its digits is 4:7. The number of such pairs is
questions.explain: Analyze digits in composition to two-digit numbers based on ratios.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: Rakesh had money to buy 8 mobile handsets of a specific company. But the retailer offered a very good discount on that particular handset. Rakesh could buy 10 mobile handsets with the amount he had. What was the discount the retailer offered?
questions.explain: Calculate discounts needed to permit purchase increases from Rakesh's spends.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: A student has to get 40% marks to pass in an examination. Suppose he gets 30 marks and fails by 30 marks, then what are the maximum marks in the examination?
questions.explain: Apply percentage rules to identify the aggregate marks indicated.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: A shopkeeper sells an article at Rs. 40 and gets X% profit. However, when he sells it at Rs. 20, he faces the same percentage of loss. What is the original cost of the article?
questions.explain: Create profit-loss equations to find discrepancies across sale amounts.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: If there is a policy that 1/3rd of the population of a community has migrated every year from one place to some other place, what is the leftover population of that community after the sixth year, if there is no further growth in the population during this period?
questions.explain: Apply geometric sequences for migratory impacts on fixed population sums.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: Gopal bought a cell phone and sold it to Ram at 10% profit. Then Ram wanted to sell it back to Gopal at 10% loss. What will be Gopal's position if he agreed?
questions.explain: Calculate price points to validate final outcomes on transactions.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: P = (40% of A) + (65% of B) and Q = (50% of A) + (50% of B), where A is greater than B. In this context which of the following statement is correct?
options: None of the above can be concluded with certainty.
questions.explain: Evaluate conditions using proportional divides regarding A and B.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: In a city, 12% of households earn less than Rs. 30,000 per year, 6% households earn more than Rs. 2,00,000 per year, 22% households earn more than Rs. 1,00,000 per year and 990 households earn between Rs. 30,000 and Rs. 1,00,000 per year. How many households earn between Rs. 1,00,000 and Rs. 2,00,000 per year?
questions.explain: Calculate totals based on given percentages and confirm households earning intervals.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: There is a milk sample with 50% water in it. If 1/3rd of this milk is added to an equal amount of pure milk, then the water in the new mixture will fall down to
questions.explain: Derive new mixture proportions based on water content and volumes of milk added.

questions.explain: Calculate total rain for four days then use averages to establish fifth-day measurements.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: The monthly incomes of X and Y are in the ratio of 4:3 and their monthly expenses are in the ratio of 3:2. However, each saves Rs. 6,000 per month. What is their total monthly income?

questions.explain: Calculate current scoring status to discern the gap to 60% benchmarks established.

questions.q: In a class, there are 18 very tall boys. If these constitute three-fourths of the boys and the total number of boys is two-thirds of the total number of students in the class, what is the number of girls in the class?
questions.explain: Establish total boys' count and project it against student totals for girls tallied.

questions.q: The monthly average salary paid to all the employees of a company was Rs. 5000. The monthly average salary paid to male and female employees was Rs. 5200 and Rs. 4200 respectively. Then the percentage of males employed in the company is
questions.explain: Work backwards using total salary averages based on statistical norms to calculate ratios.
questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: Two numbers X and Y are respectively 20% and 28% less than a third number Z. By what percentage is the number Y less than the number X?
questions.explain: Percentage evaluations are based on differencing calculated values from Z to identify Y and X ratios.

questions.q: The total emoluments of two persons are the same, but one gets allowances to the extent of 65% of his basic pay and the other gets allowances to the extent of 80% of his basic pay. The ratio of the basic pay of the former to the basic pay of the latter is:

questions.explain: Use current performance metrics to set up equations resolving the total question count.

questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: The monthly incomes Of Peter and Paul are in the ratio Of 4:3. Their expenses are in the ratio of 3:2. If each saves Rs. 6,000 at the end of the month, their monthly incomes respectively are (in Rs.)

options: Success rate is higher for women.
More men cleared the examination than women.

questions.q: A gardener increased the area of his rectangular garden by increasing its length by 40% and decreasing its width by 20%. The area of the new garden
options: is exactly the same as the old area.

questions.subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: If Sohan, while selling two goats at the same price, makes a profit of 10% on one goat and suffers a loss of 10% on the other.
options: he makes no profit and no loss.

questions.q: Out of 120 applications for a post, 70 are male and 80 have a driver's license. What is the ratio between the minimum to maximum number of males having driver's license?

questions.q: There are 100 students in a particular class. 60% students play cricket, 30% students play football and 10% students play both the games. What is the number of students who play neither cricket nor football?

questions.subject: Quantitative Ability
